correctness.rationale: Let X=ab+c. No carry under doubling would imply S_b(2X)=4S_b(X)=8X, impossible because S_b(2X)=X. With the forced carry, exact elimination from the two cycle equations gives (b^2+1)(5a-b+3)(13a-b+5)=0. The 13a+5 branch contradicts the carry; the 5a+3 branch gives c=3a+2. The converse identities and all digit bounds are explicit. The accompanying exhaustive finite check agrees with the theorem.

value.rationale: The modern literature explicitly highlights the doubling family, making its converse a motivated gap rather than an arbitrary slice. The theorem converts an infinite construction into a complete normal form on the smallest nontrivial digit stratum: the base congruence, all four digits, and uniqueness of the parameter are forced. The proof identifies carry behavior as the rigidity mechanism, providing structural information beyond a finite census.
